submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective token-identity detector at layer 0 with no contextual component (integrated gradients put 100% of the peak on the current token and 0% on the previous one, and replacing any other token leaves the peak unchanged): the pole reads the current token's embedding and returns a fixed lookup value, dominated by the word 'above' in any casing or spacing - ' above' and bare 'above' both reach 1.00 x max (1.02 here, 1.11 for '(above)' in the scan), ' Above' 0.56, 'ABOVE' 0.28 - and the word's sense is irrelevant, since physical height ('300 m above the clouds' 1.02) and document back-reference ('the above patents' 1.02) fire equally. Beyond 'above' the pole fires at 0.28-0.79 x max on a fixed, non-semantic list of specific rarer tokens: age/old words (' age' 0.87, ' old' 0.71, ' aged' 0.67, ' elderly' 0.58, ' younger' 0.53, ' young' 0.46, ' males' 0.69, ' Male' 0.62, ' Female' 0.52, ' females' 0.37), comparison/discourse words (' yet' 0.75, ' equal' 0.68, ' already' 0.50, ' hitherto' 0.53, ' over' 0.48, ' beyond' 0.47, ' towards' 0.44, ' below' 0.41, ' larger' 0.39, ' smaller' 0.35, ' farther' 0.34, ' further' 0.28), research past participles (' surveyed' 0.63, ' investigated' 0.61, ' studied' 0.58, ' explored' 0.56, ' considered' 0.55, ' examined' 0.54, ' omitted' 0.53, ' interviewed' 0.47, ' evaluated' 0.40), figure/clinical tokens ('FIG' 0.66, 'Dr' 0.50, 'FIGS' 0.47, 'Tab' 0.47, 'Rev' 0.47, ' chromosomes' 0.54, ' biopsy' 0.53, ' cirrhosis' 0.49, ' neoplastic' 0.49, ' cancer' 0.48, ' liver' 0.48) and a handful of fixed proper nouns ('Peggy' 0.62, ' TEXAS' 0.60, ' Weinstein' 0.59, ' Oslo' 0.58, ' Cobb' 0.58, ' Trevor' 0.56); a third, essentially inert band sits at 0.15-0.28 x max (' committee' 0.26, ' whole' 0.18, ' played' 0.15). Mark a text predicted active only if it contains 'above' (any case or spacing after a bracket or space) or one of the listed second-tier tokens; mark it predicted inactive otherwise, because ordinary English of every part of speech stays at or below 0.15 x max - other prepositions (' in', ' on', ' of', ' at', ' for', ' with', ' by', ' under' 0.06, ' beneath' 0.04, ' upon' 0.11), core content words, common given names and place names (' John', ' Mary', ' London', ' Paris'), comparatives (' higher', ' lower', ' more', ' greater' 0.14), formal or archaic words (' wherein' 0.08, ' thereof' 0.10, ' pursuant', ' whereby') and other rare technical nouns (' carburetor' 0.08, ' isotope', ' enzyme', ' polymerase') all stay silent, so rarity, register and part of speech alone do not predict this pole.

rival_explanations: A narrower reading: only the word 'above' is the feature and every other hit (age, old, equal, studied, males, the proper nouns) is inert tail activation of the same embedding direction, so any prompt without the token 'above' - including 'He began painting at the age of six' or 'younger males were studied' - is predicted inactive.

A broader register reading: the pole detects rare, technical or formal vocabulary as such, so ' carburetor', ' isotope', ' enzyme', ' wherein', ' thereof', ' pursuant' and other unfamiliar proper names such as ' Kosinski' or ' Gerald' should fire, with ' above' merely the most extreme instance.

A word-piece reading: apart from 'above' the pole fires on word-internal continuation fragments and common suffixes ('g', ' me', ' be', ' ge', 'ite', 'per', 'hen', 'ten' all reach 0.32-0.49 in the scan), so activity should be predicted from a token's fragment shape rather than from a word list, and long or rare words containing those fragments should fire.

![]({{ site.baseurl }}/images/voidlinux.png)
*Imagem do nosso objetivo final, com algumas coisas censuradas por conveniência. Note que, neste ponto, já havia instalado outro emulador de Terminal (o `urxvt`).*


Estou de volta, desta vez em um blog novinho em folha!
Desta vez, vou fazer um tutorial sobre como instalar uma distribuição da qual gostei bastante, chamada Void Linux. Void é uma distribuição *rolling release* como o Arch Linux, ou seja, não existe, nele, a noção de uma versão do lançamento; ter o sistema atualizado significa que você, automaticamente, tem a versão mais nova dele.
Este tutorial foi motivado pela minha necessidade de ter um manual, em Português, de como instalar uma distribuição Linux com encriptação TOTAL de disco (isto inclui a partição de *boot*, também!). Assim como eu pretendo utilizar este método adaptado para outras instalações futuras, talvez possa ser útil para mais alguém, que tenha vontade de fazer isso.
Este, também, é um tutorial que segue uma linha mais compreensiva. Não posso dizer que sou expert no assunto, mas tentarei explicar bem tudo o que faremos a cada passo, para que NÃO HAJA DÚVIDAS, e também para que você possa adaptar os passos, no futuro, para qualquer outra distribuição a seu gosto.



## "Mas já tem um tutorial sobre isso na wiki do Void Linux!"

Infelizmente, o tutorial do Void Linux é um pouco menos facilitador para novatos na área de computação. Não que você precise pensar menos ao seguir os passos que fiz, mas pretendo, aqui, expor melhor o que está acontecendo na maioria das operações cruciais.
Além disso, caso você tenha alguma sugestão sobre algo que esteja incorreto ou que possa ser uma melhoria para este tutorial, peço para que entre em contato comigo. Você poderá encontrar minhas formas de contato [na página "Sobre"]({{ site.baseurl }}/about/) ou no rodapé da página.


# Avisos

- Executei este tutorial em uma máquina virtual feita no VirtualBox, do tipo Other Linux (64-bit) e configurei-a com 1024MB de RAM e 128MB de memória de vídeo + Aceleração 3D. O disco rígido virtual possuia 20GB alocados dinamicamente. Ademais, fiz com que o VirtualBox montasse a ISO diretamente no que seria o drive de CD do mesmo;
- Eu não me responsabilizo por você fazer algo que o deixe sem SO ou que faça você perder os seus dados. Você fez porque quis. Mas, antes que isso soe como algo desmotivador: você não aprenderia nada a respeito se não tivesse feito! A sua persistência SEMPRE será a sua maior recompensa.
- O procedimento de instalação para a máquina virtual ou para o computador físico não difere em nada; você sempre vai inserir a mídia removível de alguma forma e mandar seu computador dar boot através dela. Eu não possuo, atualmente, sistemas com EFI (e, se possuísse, certamente desativaria esta opção inconveniente). How to Measure Your Portfolio's Risk
Exactly how risk is measured is a complicated issue. Before you can begin managing a portfolio you have to look at individual investments. Originally, this task was done using a calculation called the capital asset pricing model (CAPM). The CAPM is now seen more as an unrealistic view of investing, but it’s still valid as a starting point.
The CAPM leads to the use of the arbitrage pricing theory (APT), which is more flexible and has gained more favor as a functional approach to quantifying portfolio management.
Capital asset pricing model (CAPM)
Take a quick look at the CAPM equation and hopefully that will clear up CAPM and APT a bit.
rs = rf + βa(rm – rf)
rs = the rate of return demanded to invest in a specific asset
rf = the rate of return on risk-free assets
βa = the level of risk on a specific asset
rm = the rate of return on a market portfolio (an investment portfolio that perfectly matches the investment market)
By subtracting the risk-free rate from the market rate of return (which is best accomplished by investing in an index portfolio that matches something like the S&P 500), you’re determining what market premium is being offered for investing in risky assets.
In other words, the market premium is the amount of financial return you can generate by managing a market portfolio of risky assets instead of only risk-free assets. By multiplying the risk of just a specific asset, you’re calculating the risk premium being offered by a specific investment.
Because investors want a return premium that’s higher than the risk-free rate, you add the risk-free rate back into the equation, and you get the rate of returns demanded by investors to entice them to purchase an investment under CAPM.
What beta measures
The risk symbol beta (β) is not actually a measure of risk. It’s actually a statistical measure of volatility. What that means is that a particular investment can fluctuate far above normal market returns and still be considered high-risk, even though it’s making huge gains compared to the market.
Meanwhile, another investment can be consistently only 0.01 percent under market returns and still be considered low-risk, even though it’s losing value compared to the market. Beta is measured as follows:
β = [Cov(rs, rm)] / σ2m
Beta measures the amount that the value of an individual asset changes in response to a change in market value. Cov is short for covariance and refers to any movement in one variable that is inherently linked to movement in another variable.
Consider stocks for a moment. If the stock market increases by 10 percent and an individual stock increases in value 20 percent in response to the change in value of the stock market, then the beta of that particular stock is 2, or twice as volatile as the stock market itself.
So, beta doesn’t measure actual risk of loss at all, it just measures volatility. Beta is still useful, but only when used properly, which doesn’t include using it to measure

## Using the lorentz transformation for length

A surveyor measures a street to be $L=100\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m}$ long in Earth frame S. Use the Lorentz transformation to obtain an expression for its length measured from a spaceship $\text{S}\prime ,$ moving by at speed 0.20 c , assuming the x coordinates of the two frames coincide at time $t=0.$

## Solution

1. Identify the known: $L=100\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m};v=0.20c;\text{Δ}\tau =0.$
2. Identify the unknown: $L\prime \text{.}$
3. Express the answer as an equation. The surveyor in frame S has measured the two ends of the stick simultaneously, and found them at rest at ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{1}$ a distance $L={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=100\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m}$ apart. The spaceship crew measures the simultaneous location of the ends of the sticks in their frame. To relate the lengths recorded by observers in $\text{S}\prime$ and S, respectively, write the second of the four Lorentz transformation equations as:
$\begin{array}{cc}\hfill x{\prime }_{2}-x{\prime }_{1}& =\frac{{x}_{2}-vt}{\sqrt{1-{v}^{2}\text{/}{c}^{2}}}-\frac{{x}_{1}-vt}{\sqrt{1-{v}^{2}\text{/}{c}^{2}}}\hfill \\ & =\frac{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}{\sqrt{1-{v}^{2}\text{/}{c}^{2}}}=\frac{L}{\sqrt{1-{v}^{2}\text{/}{c}^{2}}}.\hfill \end{array}$
4. Do the calculation. Because $x{\prime }_{2}-x{\prime }_{1}=100\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m},$ the length of the moving stick is equal to:
$\begin{array}{cc}\hfill L\prime & =\left(100\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m}\right)\sqrt{1-{v}^{2}\text{/}{c}^{2}}\hfill \\ & =\left(100\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m}\right)\sqrt{1-{\left(0.20\right)}^{2}}\hfill \\ & =98.0\phantom{\rule{0.2em}{0ex}}\text{m.}\hfill \end{array}$

Note that the Lorentz transformation gave the length contraction equation for the street.

## Lorentz transformation and simultaneity

The observer shown in [link] standing by the railroad tracks sees the two bulbs flash simultaneously at both ends of the 26 m long passenger car when the middle of the car passes him at a speed of c /2. Find the separation in time between when the bulbs flashed as seen by the train passenger seated in the middle of the car.

## Solution

1. Identify the known: $\text{Δ}t=0.$
Note that the spatial separation of the two events is between the two lamps, not the distance of the lamp to the passenger.
2. Identify the unknown: $\text{Δ}t\prime ={t}_{2}^{\prime }-{t}_{1}^{\prime }.$
Again, note that the time interval is between the flashes of the lamps, not between arrival times for reaching the passenger.
3. Express the answer as an equation:
$\text{Δ}t=\frac{\text{Δ}t\prime +v\text{Δ}x\prime \text{/}{c}^{2}}{\sqrt{1-{v}^{2}\text{/}{c}^{2}}}.$

readings.explanation: Retrospective token-identity detector at layer 0 with no contextual component (integrated gradients put 100% of the peak on the current token and 0% on the previous one, and replacing any other token leaves the peak unchanged): the pole reads the current token's embedding and returns a fixed lookup value, dominated by the word 'above' in any casing or spacing - ' above' and bare 'above' both reach 1.00 x max (1.02 here, 1.11 for '(above)' in the scan), ' Above' 0.56, 'ABOVE' 0.28 - and the word's sense is irrelevant, since physical height ('300 m above the clouds' 1.02) and document back-reference ('the above patents' 1.02) fire equally. Beyond 'above' the pole fires at 0.28-0.79 x max on a fixed, non-semantic list of specific rarer tokens: age/old words (' age' 0.87, ' old' 0.71, ' aged' 0.67, ' elderly' 0.58, ' younger' 0.53, ' young' 0.46, ' males' 0.69, ' Male' 0.62, ' Female' 0.52, ' females' 0.37), comparison/discourse words (' yet' 0.75, ' equal' 0.68, ' already' 0.50, ' hitherto' 0.53, ' over' 0.48, ' beyond' 0.47, ' towards' 0.44, ' below' 0.41, ' larger' 0.39, ' smaller' 0.35, ' farther' 0.34, ' further' 0.28), research past participles (' surveyed' 0.63, ' investigated' 0.61, ' studied' 0.58, ' explored' 0.56, ' considered' 0.55, ' examined' 0.54, ' omitted' 0.53, ' interviewed' 0.47, ' evaluated' 0.40), figure/clinical tokens ('FIG' 0.66, 'Dr' 0.50, 'FIGS' 0.47, 'Tab' 0.47, 'Rev' 0.47, ' chromosomes' 0.54, ' biopsy' 0.53, ' cirrhosis' 0.49, ' neoplastic' 0.49, ' cancer' 0.48, ' liver' 0.48) and a handful of fixed proper nouns ('Peggy' 0.62, ' TEXAS' 0.60, ' Weinstein' 0.59, ' Oslo' 0.58, ' Cobb' 0.58, ' Trevor' 0.56); a third, essentially inert band sits at 0.15-0.28 x max (' committee' 0.26, ' whole' 0.18, ' played' 0.15). Mark a text predicted active only if it contains 'above' (any case or spacing after a bracket or space) or one of the listed second-tier tokens; mark it predicted inactive otherwise, because ordinary English of every part of speech stays at or below 0.15 x max - other prepositions (' in', ' on', ' of', ' at', ' for', ' with', ' by', ' under' 0.06, ' beneath' 0.04, ' upon' 0.11), core content words, common given names and place names (' John', ' Mary', ' London', ' Paris'), comparatives (' higher', ' lower', ' more', ' greater' 0.14), formal or archaic words (' wherein' 0.08, ' thereof' 0.10, ' pursuant', ' whereby') and other rare technical nouns (' carburetor' 0.08, ' isotope', ' enzyme', ' polymerase') all stay silent, so rarity, register and part of speech alone do not predict this pole.

A narrower reading: only the word 'above' is the feature and every other hit (age, old, equal, studied, males, the proper nouns) is inert tail activation of the same embedding direction, so any prompt without the token 'above' - including 'He began painting at the age of six' or 'younger males were studied' - is predicted inactive.

A broader register reading: the pole detects rare, technical or formal vocabulary as such, so ' carburetor', ' isotope', ' enzyme', ' wherein', ' thereof', ' pursuant' and other unfamiliar proper names such as ' Kosinski' or ' Gerald' should fire, with ' above' merely the most extreme instance.

A word-piece reading: apart from 'above' the pole fires on word-internal continuation fragments and common suffixes ('g', ' me', ' be', ' ge', 'ite', 'per', 'hen', 'ten' all reach 0.32-0.49 in the scan), so activity should be predicted from a token's fragment shape rather than from a word list, and long or rare words containing those fragments should fire.
